lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Building a Fueling Meal
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: meal variety

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice meal variety. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: With an adult, the learner looks at a small set of available no-heat ingredients spanning at least three food groups and practices combining them two different ways, then builds a third combination independently that's meaningfully different from the first two.
safetyNotes: No heat source is used; ingredients are chosen to be safe for independent handling.

simulationAlternative.description: If a varied set of real ingredients isn't available, the learner instead plans three different combinations in writing from a provided list of ingredients spanning multiple food groups, describing each combination and its food groups instead of physically assembling it.

materials: learner-local: a small set of no-heat ingredients spanning at least three food groups

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Which of your three combinations would you actually want to eat again, and why — taste, how it made you feel, or something else?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Variety across combinations: At least two of three combinations use a meaningfully different food-group mix. | Reflection on preference vs. variety: Reflection names at least one non-taste factor, like how it made them feel. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Plan a fourth combination that uses an ingredient the learner rarely chooses, and reflect on what made that ingredient a less automatic pick.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice meal variety. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: meal variety worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With an adult, the learner looks at a small set of available no-heat ingredients spanning at least three food groups and practices combining them two different ways, then builds a third combination independently that's meaningfully different from the first two.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact meal variety decision or action.
Model move 2: Before building anything, name the food groups you can see represented in today's ingredients (for example: grain, protein, fruit or vegetable, dairy).
Model move 3: With your adult, build two different meal combinations from the same ingredient set, using a different food-group mix each time.

Model check: Variety across combinations: At least two of three combinations use a meaningfully different food-group mix. | Reflection on preference vs. variety: Reflection names at least one non-taste factor, like how it made them feel.

resources.title: meal variety action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for meal variety.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: meal variety coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With an adult, the learner looks at a small set of available no-heat ingredients spanning at least three food groups and practices combining them two different ways, then builds a third combination independently that's meaningfully different from the first two.
Coach direction: Before building anything, name the food groups you can see represented in today's ingredients (for example: grain, protein, fruit or vegetable, dairy).
Learner prompt: List the food groups you see.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: meal variety complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, build two different meal combinations from the same ingredient set, using a different food-group mix each time.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My first combination used at least three food groups.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My second combination was meaningfully different from the first, not just the same foods rearranged.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult and I talked through why variety across food groups is useful, not just why it tastes different.

Equal-access rule: If a varied set of real ingredients isn't available, the learner instead plans three different combinations in writing from a provided list of ingredients spanning multiple food groups, describing each combination and its food groups instead of physically assembling it.

resources.title: meal variety minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which of your three combinations would you actually want to eat again, and why — taste, how it made you feel, or something else?

Success checks: Variety across combinations: At least two of three combinations use a meaningfully different food-group mix. | Reflection on preference vs. variety: Reflection names at least one non-taste factor, like how it made them feel.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: meal variety supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional meal variety condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Variety across combinations: At least two of three combinations use a meaningfully different food-group mix. | Reflection on preference vs. variety: Reflection names at least one non-taste factor, like how it made them feel..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: meal variety — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
With your adult, build two different meal combinations from the same ingredient set, using a different food-group mix each time.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: meal variety — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If a varied set of real ingredients isn't available, the learner instead plans three different combinations in writing from a provided list of ingredients spanning multiple food groups, describing each combination and its food groups instead of physically assembling it.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Variety across combinations: At least two of three combinations use a meaningfully different food-group mix. | Reflection on preference vs. variety: Reflection names at least one non-taste factor, like how it made them feel.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u04-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
